questions.prompt: What scope of fix do you want?
questions.description: The session showed four symptoms (tool-result spin, empty-result ignored, viz failure, post-timeout unresponsiveness). Pick which ones this goal should address.
questions.recommendedAnswer: All four: stuck-loop detection, empty-result strategy shift, tool-failure self-diagnosis, and timeout recovery. They're all facets of the same root issue (no progress detection + no resilient failure handling).

options.label: Stuck-loop detection (repeated similar tool calls)
Empty/duplicate tool-result strategy shift
Tool-failure self-diagnosis (e.g. Portal not opening)
Post-timeout session unresponsiveness

questions.prompt: How should the agent detect it's stuck?
questions.description: Mechanism for recognizing no progress is being made.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Hybrid: hash recent tool-call signatures (tool + args) and flag when the last N calls have low diversity, combined with checking if tool results are non-empty and new. This catches both 'repeating the same search' and 'getting back nothing useful'.

options.label: Hash recent (tool, args) pairs — flag low diversity
Embed tool args and compare — slower but semantically aware
Compare new tool results to prior results — flag no-new-info
All three layered together

questions.prompt: What should happen when the agent detects it's stuck?
questions.description: How aggressive should the recovery be?
questions.recommendedAnswer: Inject a corrective user message: 'You've called the same tool N times with similar args and are not making progress. Try a fundamentally different approach: use a different tool, simplify the question, or answer from what you know.' Then allow one more attempt. If still stuck, terminate the turn with an explanation.

options.label: Inject corrective user-message and allow N more retries
Forbid the repeated tool on next attempt (hard block)
Skip remaining depth, force synthesis from existing results
Stop the turn and ask the user for guidance

questions.prompt: How should timeout-induced unresponsiveness be handled?
questions.description: The session went dead after [timeout waiting for response]. This is a protocol/transport issue, not a logic one.
questions.recommendedAnswer: The agent-loop (Clojure side) should have a watchdog: if no state change occurs in N seconds, kill the in-flight LLM call, reset the message queue, and surface a 'session was unresponsive' error to the user via the :on-error callback. The CLI should not deadlock waiting on a never-delivered promise.

options.label: Clojure-side watchdog with hard timeout on LLM call + queue reset
Wrap deliver-response in a timeout with fallback error
Periodic heartbeat from the LLM client that the loop checks

questions.prompt: Should the visualize tool get self-diagnostic improvements?
questions.description: The repl-eval+visualize path silently produced no output. The agent should know when Portal isn't actually displaying.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Yes — the visualize tool should return a structured result that includes (1) whether Portal was successfully opened/connected, (2) the data hash so the agent can confirm it was submitted, and (3) a hint to the user to check the Portal window if submission succeeded. The agent loop should treat 'visualize called, no portal detected' as a recoverable error, not silent success.

options.label: Return structured {:portal-open? :data-submitted? :hint} from visualize
Verify Portal is actually rendering (e.g. via Portal API health check)
Skip Portal entirely — just print to terminal or write to file

questions.prompt: Where in the architecture should this live?
questions.description: The new interceptor architecture (chain.clj, interceptors.clj) is the natural place for cross-cutting loop concerns.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Add a new :guard slot interceptor 'stuck-loop-detector' (interceptors.clj) that runs in :enter, computes a signature hash of recent tool calls, and when stuck is detected, enqueues a corrective guidance stage. Timeout watchdog goes in agent-loop (loop.clj) since it's a transport concern. Portal diagnostics are tool-local (tools/portal.clj).

options.label: New :guard slot interceptor in interceptors.clj + tool-local fixes
Modify llm-turn / process-messages directly in loop.clj
Add as a new plugin (plugins/stuck_loop.clj) so it's opt-in

questions.description: How should we verify the new behavior?
questions.recommendedAnswer: All four: parity tests for stuck-loop detection (scripted LLM that repeats the same call), unit tests for the hash/similarity function, integration test for timeout watchdog (simulated hung LLM client), and a Portal mock that returns a structured result.

options.label: Parity tests (scripted LLM that simulates stuck behavior)
Unit tests for detection fn (hash, signature comparison)
Integration test for timeout watchdog with mocked hung LLM
Mock Portal client that returns structured :portal-open? status

questions.recommendedAnswer: No changes to memory backend, no LLM provider swap, no new web-search backend, no work on the test-isolation Datalevin corruption issue (that's pre-existing and separate).

options.label: No memory backend / Datalevin changes
No LLM provider changes (keep :openai-compatible default)
No fix for the pre-existing test-runner Datalevin corruption
No new tools — only modifications to existing ones
